newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels say S.African envoys met Kabila.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels say S.African envoys met Kabila.

text.p: Zairean rebels said on Friday envoys of South African President Nelson Mandela met their leader Laurent Kabila in rebel-held territory to pave the way for negotiations to end the war with the government.
The envoys arrived in the eastern border town of Goma on Wednesday, said Kakudji Gaetan, foreign affairs commissar of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (AFDL).
They met Kabila in Goma, Kakudji told reporters. He did not say when the meeting took place.
"They came here to make contact with us and to make possible the start of negotiations," Kakudji said. "Negotiations will concern the passing of power but not our surrender."
The AFDL says it will negotiate but insists that Zaire's ailing president Mobutu Sese Seko show a firm commitment to taking part.
Kabila made a diplomatic breakthrough in his search for recognition when Mandela received him in Johannesburg on February 26, but even then he turned down Mandela's request for a ceasefire.
"Given his international stature Mandela is the person indicated to mediate between the parties in the conflict in Zaire," Kakudji said.
Diplomats said Kabila met United Nations special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun on Thursday in the northern Ugandan town of Gulu but again rejected U.N. pleas for a ceasefire.
Zairean rebels who control at least one-fifth of the country after a campaign starting last October are advancing on Zaire's third city Kisangani.
